subject: Access trace egress windows & preservation commitments
messages:
From: Carol Baxter <carol.baxter@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access traces — on-demand egress window question

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from our security team as we go through the integration checklist: we need clarity on on-demand egress windows for access traces. Specifically:
- Do you support an ad-hoc export request (customer-initiated) within a 24‑hour SLA?
- What guarantees are there that the exported files will contain unaltered timestamps, UID mappings, and the full trace (not sampled)?
- Are exports delivered encrypted in transit and at rest, and can you sign an evidence attestation for a single export event?

We'd like to document the approach in our audit pack for the board review next week. If you can point to the exact timeline and any limits (daily export size, retention of exported copies on your side), that would help.

Thanks,
Carol Baxter
Head of Security, Acme Health

[Attachment: request-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Baxter <carol.baxter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access traces — on-demand egress window question

Hi Carol — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:
- Yes, we support customer-initiated on-demand exports; standard SLA for delivery of a completed export package is 48 hours for typical datasets, 24 hours is possible for small scope requests and is treated as an expedited request.
- Exports are full (no sampling) by default for tenant-level audit/access traces; we preserve original event timestamps and internal identifiers in the export manifest.
- All exports are delivered over TLS and we provide an AES-256 encrypted archive. We can provide a signed attestation certifying the export event (time window, files generated) as part of the package.

A few notes & constraints to call out:
- Expedited (24h) requests are subject to an approval/fee when the dataset exceeds ~100GB or when there are cross-region egress policy checks.
- We retain a transient staging copy of the export for 14 days to support re-transmission if a transfer fails; we can delete the staging copy on request immediately after delivery and include that as an attested action in the certificate.
- Exports include a machine-readable manifest (JSONL) and a human-readable index (CSV). We attach a small sample in this thread.

I'll loop in Karthik for any residency/region checks and Marissa for legal/attestation wording. If you want 24-hour SLA for this specific request, please indicate dataset scope and region (US/EU/APAC).

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: export-sample-manifest.jsonl (sample), note: sample contains redacted UIDs]

From: legal@acmehealth.com
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access traces — on-demand egress window question

Vanessa / Marissa,

A couple of legal clarifications before we mark this as acceptable:
1) We need confirmation that exported archives are not persisted by Redwood beyond the 14‑day transient staging period unless explicitly requested in writing. Please confirm the exact deletion workflow and whether a tamper-evident deletion confirmation can be provided.
2) Can Redwood include a signed hash (SHA-256) for each delivered archive and include the signing key metadata in the attestation?
3) For cross-border exports (EU -> US), please confirm if Redwood will run any additional checks and whether there are predictable hold times for export approval.

Happy to sign an NDA addendum if you need to exchange private KMS fingerprints.

Regards,
Acme Health Legal

[Attachment: export-legal-questions.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Baxter <carol.baxter@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access traces — on-demand egress window question

Hi Carol / Acme Legal — thanks, a few concrete confirmations from the infra side: 

1) Deletion workflow: after export generation we keep the encrypted archive in a transient S3-like staging area for up to 14 days. Deletion request (customer-initiated) triggers an automated workflow: archive is shredded (cryptographic erase of object keys) and an audit event is written to the tenant audit store recording deletion time, operator (system), and request id. We can deliver a signed deletion certificate (timestamp + SHA-256 of archive file prior to deletion) within 24 hours of the request.

2) Signed hashes: yes — we compute SHA-256 for each archive and sign the digest with a Redwood export-signing key. We can provide the public key fingerprint in the attestation. If you require KMS-to-KMS wrap (customer-provided key), we support envelope encryption where the final archive is encrypted with a customer KMS key prior to delivery; in that case Redwood will not retain plaintext key material and will still provide the signed SHA-256 of the ciphertext.

3) Cross-border: for EU -> non-EU exports there is an automated policy gate. Typical hold time is under 6 hours for standard business requests; if manual approval is required (e.g., highly sensitive regulated records) the export will be queued and we surface estimated hold time in the request ticket. We can include a policy note in the attestation that records the final approval path and timestamps.

Next steps: Vanessa — if Acme confirms scope (date range + tenant id + target region) we'll open an expedited export ticket and provision the helpdesk SLA. I'll attach the short playbook describing the export package contents and the attestation templates.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Security (Redwood Inference)

[Attachments: egress-playbook.pdf (policy/playbook), sample-audit-logs.tar.gz (sample logs)]
